analysis.title: GS Dunn - GS US Daily Download 9 Oct 2026
key_insights: Despite the S&P 500 falling 0.5% on 8 Oct, 70% of stocks in the index finished higher. RTY outperformed SPX, which outperformed NDX. The S&P 500 vs S&P ex AI divergence is now nearly 10%.

Fed Governor Waller said he likely expects two additional rate hikes to be appropriate. He cited no resolution to the Middle East conflict, AI buildout raising consumer prices for technology goods, and the risk of new tariffs.

GS continues to expect one additional 25bp hike in December. GS lowered its probability that the FOMC passes on a December hike, because Waller's speech is a hawkish shift relative to his earlier emphasis on the three-month annualized core PCE rate, which is now 2.0%.
GS upgrades Palantir to Buy from Neutral with a 12-month price target of $230 (18% upside). The stock is +16% YTD vs NDX +24% and trades at a discount to growth comps on EV/FCF.

Palantir debates: whether the AI opportunity is already realized (current $8bn revenue run rate, ~100% growth), and whether the forward deployed engineer (FDE) model is sustainable. GS argues the addressable market is deepening through sovereign AI, bespoke applications and verticalization, and that AI-automated FDEs sustain the lead.
GS Americas Energy lists 10 stock ideas into Q4 across four themes: oil E&P (COP, OXY, PR), power and LNG (PWR, DUK, BKR, GLNG), refining (DINO), and natural gas upstream and midstream (TRP, AR).
PepsiCo Q3 organic sales growth was +3.1% vs GS/VA consensus +2.9% and +2.4% in Q2. Volumes were +0.5% vs +1% in Q2. EPS was $2.34 (+2.5% y/y) vs GS/FactSet consensus $2.31/$2.30.

PepsiCo narrowed FY26 organic sales growth guidance to ~+3% (prior +2%-4%) and cut constant-currency EPS growth guidance to +1-2% (prior low end of +4%-6%). GS says the cut was largely expected and the stock is +2.5%.

The trading floor saw choppy, top-down trading. ETF share of volume was ~32%, the highest since June. Headlines were 'Trump: not be attacking Iran at any time prior to the midterm' and 'OpenAI annualised revenue $20B less than previously signalled', after which GS saw long-only and hedge fund supply in large cap tech.

Semis and AI weakness also came from underwhelming Samsung and TSM prints vs high expectations, reports that major AI players (ORCL, AVGO, SCPX) plan to tap debt markets further, and no update on the China optical ban weighing on COHR, LITE and GLW.
RTY held its 200-day moving average as yields fell in the afternoon, snapping a 4-day streak of underperformance vs SPX.
GS floor activity was a 4 on a 1-10 scale, finishing -686bps better for sale, driven by overlapping supply in macro expressions and large cap tech.
CMG rose 8% and SBUX fell 160bps on headlines that Starbucks explored a takeover of Chipotle, which would be the biggest restaurant sector deal ever. SBUX CEO Brian Niccol was formerly CEO of CMG.

Healthcare weakened with XLV giving back its prior-day outperformance. GS cites no clear cause but names ARGX -12%, reversion in Tools after peak AI drug discovery euphoria, and managed care jitters ahead of imminent Medicare STARs ratings.
Post-bell, HUM rose 12% on Medicare STARs results. T, VZ and TMUS fell about 3% after hours on a report that SpaceX is to buy a nationwide low-band spectrum license portfolio.
